subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and if so what are the accepted activity source, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, and user-visible notification behavior?
rationale: The remaining work is not a small bug patch: it adds recovery policy, config/default behavior, mutating child-run control, and channel/user-visible failure handling for existing deployments.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default/opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to the session activity and kill/reap items.

options.title: Prototype as default-off
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in watchdog first, with focused live proof and no behavior change for existing installs until maintainers accept defaults.

options.title: Defer to existing controls
options.body: Do not add automatic nudge/kill yet; rely on runTimeoutSeconds plus a future manual kill/reap surface and revisit only with more production evidence.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default/opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to the session activity and kill/reap items.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the subagent registry/control boundary and adjacent timeout semantics.
